summary: OpenAI publishes enterprise guidance on managing AI spend and adoption for ChatGPT Work, covering usage visibility, evaluating model ROI, governance of agentic workflows, and matching capacity products to demand.

mechanisms.reason: The document cites a stated efficiency figure showing fewer tokens and less time needed for comparable or better task performance.
mechanisms.quote: GPT‑5.6 ⁠ continues that progress, delivering better performance in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 54% fewer output tokens and 57% less time per task.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI frames enterprise usage as shifting from chat to longer-running, tool-using agentic workflows requiring new governance and capacity products.
mechanisms.quote: This becomes more important as teams adopt plugins, connectors, Computer Use, and other frontier capabilities that can operate across enterprise systems.

practices.reason: Gives a concrete measurement method -- evals on real tasks with a defined 'good enough' bar and cost-per-accepted-outcome tracking -- that a team could run directly.
practices.quote: Use evals that reflect real tasks ⁠ , including edge cases, and define “good enough” before testing. Then measure the full cost of reaching that standard: model and tool usage, attempts, completion rate, latency, and human review.

practices.reason: New admin console usage analytics and spend controls change how enterprise teams monitor and manage their API/product integration.
practices.quote: Updated usage analytics and spend controls ⁠ in the Admin Console help admins see adoption, credit usage, and spend by user, product, and model; track trends over time; identify emerging patterns; and understand when usage reflects broad adoption, a power-user workflow, or a recurring business process that may deserve more investment.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 is stated to deliver better coding-agent benchmark performance with fewer tokens and less time per task, a stated capability and cost/latency improvement.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.6 ⁠ continues that progress, delivering better performance in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 54% fewer output tokens and 57% less time per task.

practices.reason: Describes prompt and context management practices (stopping conditions, focused tools) that reduce loops and wasted spend, but without a stated quantitative gain.
practices.quote: Clear instructions, focused tools, reusable context, and explicit stopping conditions can reduce loops and wasted spend.

practices.reason: Mentions Batch API, Flex processing, and Prompt Caching as options for cost-efficient serving but does not describe a technique or quantify a gain.
practices.quote: Batch API , Flex processing , or Prompt Caching ⁠ for asynchronous work or repeated context.
